EICRs, Testing and Fault Finding in Crawley, Surrey and Sussex

We carry out electrical installation condition reports (EICRs) on homes and businesses, test emergency lighting, and trace and fix faults, including emergency call outs. A typical domestic EICR takes about 1 to 4 hours.

Call 07813 626998 WhatsApp Us

Domestic EICRs, in Working Hours

A typical domestic EICR takes about 1 to 4 hours, depending on the size of the property, the number of circuits and the state of the installation, and we do them in working hours. It's worth having one when you buy or sell a house, when you let a property, or when the installation hasn't been inspected for several years.

Commercial EICRs, Usually Out of Hours

A commercial EICR takes 2 to 10 hours. Because the power has to go off, we usually do them out of hours. Landlords, property managers, insurers and businesses often need one, and an outdated board, repeat faults or damaged accessories are signs one is due. On Ship Street in East Grinstead we carried out a 5 year EICR and the emergency lighting tests on an architects office; a yearly emergency lighting test takes about 3 hours.

A Clear Report You Can Act On

Scott's view is that some inspections get rushed, the reports are vague, and work gets recommended without a reason. We test thoroughly, write a clear report, explain what we found and tell you what work, if any, is needed.

The business holds NAPIT certificates for periodic inspection and testing of dwellings and of other buildings, and test and inspection is one of the team's qualifications.

Faults and Emergency Call Outs

We traced and fixed a fault for a customer in RH10 who wrote on Checkatrade that the engineer arrived on time and solved the issue very quickly. In East Grinstead we answered an emergency call out to a shop on London Road. Leon, a repeat customer, has had everything from fault finding to a full rewire from us.

How Long It Takes, and Prices

  • A domestic EICR: about 1 to 4 hours, in working hours
  • A commercial EICR: 2 to 10 hours, usually out of hours
  • A yearly emergency lighting test: about 3 hours

When an Inspection Is Due

General signs, not a diagnosis. If you spot one, call us and we will talk it through.

  • Circuits that trip again and again
  • Damaged or scorched sockets and switches
  • An old fuseboard
  • No inspection for several years, or a sale or new tenancy coming up

Useful to Tell Us

  • The type of property and roughly how big
  • Whether it is a rental, a sale, a business or your own home
  • When it was last tested, if you know
